slides.texte_overlay:
5 posture mistakes that kill
your charisma in public
Mistake 1: leaning on everything. Walls, tables, doorframes. It looks tired and bored. Stand on your own two feet and you instantly look awake and engaged.
Mistake 2: pushing your head forward. Hours on your phone pull your chin out in front of your chest. Tuck it back gently and stack your head right over your shoulders.
Mistake 3: turning your body away while you talk. Point your feet and chest toward the person. Even with perfect words, a body facing away says you want to leave.
Mistake 4: sitting slumped on the sofa at a party. Sink into the cushions and you disappear. Sit forward a little, back straight, and you're part of the room.
Before: tense and hunched, head full of noise. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, a calmer mind and a body that finally relaxes in public.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: tense and hunched, head full of noise. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Calmer mind, relaxed body.

slides.texte_overlay: Mistake 5: tiny, nervous steps. Short quick steps look anxious. Take longer, slower strides with your shoulders relaxed. Your walk alone can change how people see you.
The fix: film yourself walking and talking for one minute. It feels strange, but you'll spot your own habits instantly, and seeing them is half of fixing them.
